name: Kang-Petrov Arms KPM-15R 'Reclaim'
description:
The KPM-15R Reclaim is a precision rifle designed specifically for urban resistance operations in built environments. The weapon chambers 7.62mm caseless with a barrel length optimized for engagements between 200 and 500 meters — the typical ranges encountered when shooting between buildings, across intersections, and through urban canyons. The scope is a fixed 6x optic with an illuminated reticle optimized for the geometric regularity of urban environments.

The Reclaim's distinguishing feature is its rapid-displacement design. The weapon breaks down into three components — barrel assembly, receiver, and stock — in under 10 seconds without tools, and reassembles in 15. This allows the marksman to break the weapon down into pieces that fit inside a common backpack, move to a new position through public spaces without displaying a rifle, and reassemble at the new firing position. The quick-disconnect system maintains zero — the weapon shoots to the same point of aim after reassembly.

Kang-Petrov markets the Reclaim openly as a resistance weapon, making no pretense about its intended use case. At Φ3,000, it is affordable for organized resistance movements, and its rapid-displacement capability allows urban marksmen to maintain operational tempo in environments where static positions are quickly identified and neutralized.
specifications:
caliber: 7.62mm caseless
effective_range: 500m (urban optimized for 200-500m)
rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic
magazine_capacity: 15 rounds
weight: 4.0 kg
tactical_use: The Reclaim enables shoot-and-move tactics in urban environments. The marksman fires from a position, breaks the weapon down in 10 seconds, moves through public spaces as a civilian, and reassembles at a new position for the next engagement. This displacement cycle makes the marksman extremely difficult to locate and neutralize, as the weapon disappears between engagements. The zero-maintaining quick-disconnect ensures accuracy is preserved through repeated assembly cycles.
cultural_context: The Reclaim is the weapon of urban insurgency. Its design explicitly enables the tactics that make urban resistance effective — appearing from nowhere, striking, and vanishing into the civilian population. Corporate security forces view the Reclaim as a threat to stability. Resistance movements view it as a tool of liberation. Kang-Petrov views it as a product that sells itself to customers who have no other options.
story_hooks: A Reclaim marksman has been engaging corporate security from a different position each day for two weeks. The weapon breaks down so quickly that every search of the surrounding buildings finds nothing. Corporate security knows the weapon exists but cannot locate it between engagements.

Kang-Petrov's Reclaim production data was leaked, revealing the serial numbers of every unit shipped to a specific resistance movement. The corponation now knows exactly how many Reclaims the resistance has — but not where they are.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, modular precision rifle with a distinctly urban aesthetic. The Reclaim presents as a purposeful tool rather than a military instrument—clean lines, minimalist ergonomics, and an overall silhouette that emphasizes modularity. The fixed 6x scope sits forward on the receiver in a way that suggests geometric precision. Despite its capability, it carries an almost civilian intentionality.
physical_description.dimensions: Assembled length: 94 cm | Barrel: 41 cm | Receiver: 38 cm | Stock: 28 cm | Width across charging handle: 6.5 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and manageable at 4.0 kg assembled—hefty enough to feel substantial, light enough for sustained shooting positions or rapid repositioning. The modular design distributes weight intuitively when separated.
physical_description.primary_material: Polymer composite receiver with reinforced aluminum quick-disconnect nodes. Barrel assembly is chromoly steel. Stock is carbon-fiber reinforced polymer with steel locking lugs.
physical_description.finish: Matte graphite-gray polymer body with brushed aluminum junction points. The barrel wears a subdued dark nitrile coating. Quick-disconnect nodes gleam with precision machining—deliberate visual emphasis on the tool's core mechanic.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte graphite-gray primary with brushed aluminum accents at disconnect points. The illuminated reticle housing is dark gunmetal. Minimal branding in muted gold lettering.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with subtle honeycomb pattern for secure purchase without being ostentatious. The charging handle is wrapped in thin rubberized material for quiet operation.
distinctive_features: Visible quick-disconnect bayonet lugs at barrel-to-receiver and receiver-to-stock junctions—precision-engineered, color-matched to the finish
Fixed 6x scope with illuminated reticle featuring urban geometry-optimized crosshairs (nested grid pattern rather than traditional crosshair)
Charging handle positioned for rapid manipulation during disassembly
Magazine well features quick-release paddle visible on the left side
Serial plate mounted on receiver with Kang-Petrov Arms logo and 'RECLAIM' designation in sans-serif font
Minimal rail system—only top-mounted, leaving sides and bottom uncluttered to facilitate packing into tight spaces
Heat vents along the barrel shroud in a subtle linear pattern
Witness marks engraved near quick-disconnect points—subtle alignment guides for rapid reassembly
Sling attachment points integrated into the quick-disconnect system itself
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Kang-Petrov Arms logo (circular compass-like symbol merging Cyrillic and Latin characters) stamped on the left side of the receiver. 'KPM-15R RECLAIM' printed in gold lettering below the scope rail. Serial number on a stainless steel plate inset into the receiver. Manufacturing origin mark: 'GLMZ-LICENSED' on the barrel assembly near the muzzle.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-maintained and operational. Finish shows minimal wear despite regular use—matte surfaces are designed to resist reflection and visible damage. Quick-disconnect nodes may show minor scuffing from repeated assembly cycles, but this is expected wear. No rust or corrosion. Optic glass is clean and clear. Overall impression: a tool in regular, professional use—not pristine, not weathered.
